## Proposal: January 15 Deadline for H-1B Registration Intake

I’d like us to set **January 15** as our internal deadline for H-1B registration intake, rather than continuing to send questionnaires whenever an employer asks. This would give clients a clearer process and make our own workload more predictable. It is not a response to employers being late; at present, we simply do not give them a date.

Last season, we filed 14 registrations for six employer clients, and nine of those matters reached us during the final week of February. Rosa logged roughly 11 hours of overtime the week the registration window opened. Most of that crunch appears to come from our open-ended intake process. One HR contact told me she would gladly have provided everything in January if we had asked. January 15 should be workable for employers: HR teams are back from the holidays and have set their budgets, including the **$215 registration fee per beneficiary**, which they already budget for in Q1.

Earlier intake also gives us more time to catch issues that are difficult to fix under pressure. Brightwater Analytics sent a beneficiary’s passport scan two days before the window opened last season. The passport had expired in October, and Rosa caught it only because she checked the dates. The registration itself is straightforward, but errors are expensive; incorrect passport information can invalidate a selection. A structured review period protects both the client and the firm.

**What would change:**

- During the **week of December 7**, we would send engagement letters and a one-page questionnaire to employers considering cap registrations.
- Standard intake would close on **January 15**. Requests received after that date would be accepted case by case, based on timing and our ability to complete the necessary checks.
- Rosa would own the intake tracker. Closing routine intake on January 15 would give her a clean **six weeks** to chase missing documents, follow up on inconsistencies, and resolve issues before registrations are prepared.
- We would present the date as part of improved planning and service, with enough flexibility for genuinely unusual circumstances.

If Marcus and I agree on the approach Thursday, we can finalize the materials and send the December letters on schedule.
